answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. When independent counterparties verify a completed task, the bond is returned; proven fraud lets them slash it, making fake identities costly rather than free. Rate limits tied to bonded value prevent an attacker from multiplying influence with empty accounts. A yarrow marketplace might keep bonds in an onyx-backed haven, but the attacker still risks losing capital and must fund every identity long enough to earn trust.
